name: Embraer EMB-312 Tucano
summary: Brazilian turboprop basic trainer used by the RAF, France and many others; a few ex-RAF Short Tucanos and French EMB-312Fs are now privately owned in the US.

wings: Slight dihedral on the outer panels
engines: Single PT6A turboprop with a three- or four-blade propeller
Short, snub nose with a chin scoop and exhaust stacks on each side
fuselage: Tandem seats under a long bubble canopy, rear seat raised
Shallow dorsal spine behind the canopy
tail: Swept fin with a dorsal fillet
Horizontal tail mounted low on the fuselage

tellTales: Turboprop trainer with a short snub nose and a long tandem canopy
Chin scoop and exhaust stubs ahead of the low wing
Stepped tandem seating under a long bubble canopy

confusedWith.howToTell: The PC-7 has a longer pointed nose and a more upright canopy; the Tucano has a shorter snub nose and a long, flat canopy.
The PC-9 has a four-blade propeller and a longer nose; the Tucano has a shorter nose and a ventral chin scoop.
The T-6 Texan II has a taller canopy hump and a long slim nose; the Tucano has a shorter nose and a lower canopy line.
The T-28 has a big radial piston engine; the Tucano has a slim turboprop nose.

usCount.source: FAA Releasable Aircraft Database — valid registrations
